title: Generalized Linear Bandits with Memory
claim: Memory-dependent transformations of a fixed preference vector make the optimal action drift over time, producing endogenous non-stationarity.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, timeline arrow with round labels beneath
description: Four spheres sit side by side, one per round (t, t+1, t+2, t+3), and a gray timeline arrow with round labels runs beneath them. Each sphere has 3D-style axes and a purple-to-light-blue gradient that shows the expected reward over actions. A bold red arrow from the origin is the preference vector A_{t-1}θ*, A_tθ*, and so on, with the matrix subscript changing from panel to panel. A dotted line connects the arrow tip to a dark purple dot on the sphere surface, which marks the optimal arm. The arrow rotates from right to upper-left across the panels. The darkest purple region follows it, so the best action changes each round. The eye goes first to the red arrows and the purple hotspots.
caption: Illustration of how nonstationary preferences are modeled in the bandit with memory setting. The sphere represents the action space, and the red arrow denotes the preference vector Aθ∗. The preference vector is transformed by a memory matrix that depends on previously selected arm features, resulting in different optimal arms at each round. The color gradient visualizes the distribution of expected rewards over actions at each round: actions in darker purple regions yield higher rewards, whereas those in lighter blue regions yield lower rewards.
abstract: We study generalized linear bandits with memory, an endogenous non-stationary setting in which rewards depend on past actions through a finite memory matrix. Building on prior work for linear models (Clerici et al., 2024), we show that the previously known $\tilde{O}(T^{3/4})$ regret bound stems from a loose analysis, and we provide a sharpened analysis that recovers a $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ regret rate in the linear case. We then extend this improvement to generalized linear models and propose a block-wise algorithm based on shrunken confidence bounds. Our algorithm achieves a regret bound of $\tilde{O}\left(\sqrt{mT} + d\sqrt{T} + \sqrtÎº\, d^{2} m^{1/4} T^{1/4} + Îºd^{2} \right)$, where $d$ denotes the feature dimension, $m$ the memory length, and $Îº$ a curvature parameter of the link function. This attains a $\sqrt{T}$-type rate despite nonlinear rewards and memory effects. To the best of our knowledge, this analysis provides a unified treatment of memory-induced non-stationarity and nonlinear link functions, while ensuring that the leading regret term is independent of the curvature of the link function. We conduct numerical experiments that are consistent with our theoretical findings.
